title: Automated decay detection and archival policy for verified performance profiles
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Problem: As models evolve and traffic patterns shift, some Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost signatures) degrade in accuracy or become stale. Without an automated detection and lifecycle policy we risk serving incorrect guidance (bad pinning, cost underestimates) and unnecessarily cluttering the catalog with deprecated artifacts.

Goal: Build an end-to-end playbook and automation that: (1) detects statistical decay in verified profiles, (2) marks profiles for archival/retirement with clear reasons, (3) triggers backfill evaluation for missing or unverified model variants, and (4) surfaces actionable signals in the Console and downstream verification pipelines.

Scope:
- Decay detection: implement an alerting rule that compares live telemetry (P95 latency, tokens/sec, failed-op rate, cost-per-token) against the canonical verified profile using sliding-window drift metrics (14- and 90-day).
- Archival policy: define states (active, flagged, archived, deprecated) and automated transitions with human-in-the-loop gates for high-impact profiles.
- Backfill/retrospective verification: queue missing model-version/quantization combinations for re-run of verification harness when capacity exists.
- UX: add a profile health badge and historical trend sparkline to the perf profile detail page plus an opt-in notification for profile stewards.
- Integrations: wire to verification CI, profile git-backed registry, cost-normalization service, and incident runbooks.

Success metrics:
- 95% of decay candidates identified within 7 days of measurable divergence.
- Reduce manual stale profile reviews by 60% in Q2.
- Backfill queue completion time median <= 21 days for high-priority profiles.

Non-goals: Automated rollback of customer pinning (must remain manual) and aggressive auto-deletion of historically important profiles (archival not irreversible deletion).
comments: 2025-02-12 - Sana Patel: Created ticket to centralize decay detection. Initial draft attachment in Drive. Requested engineering feasibility assessment.
2025-02-18 - Eng feedback (Nina Rodriguez): Sliding-window approach sounds good; recommend using weighted EWMA for cost metrics to be less noisy. Will prototype in verification-metrics service.
2025-02-21 - Design review (Tom Becker): UI proposals attached. Suggest timeline sparkline with change annotations (canary, release) to help stewards correlate shifts.
2025-02-25 - Decision: Use two-tier threshold: soft-warning (7% deviation p95 or 10% cost variance) vs hard-flag (15% deviation p95 or 25% cost variance). Metrics team to surface both in health API.

2025-02-27 - Implementation note (Liam O'Connor): Creating backfill queue consumer that rates limits to verification CI capacity. Prioritization: customer-facing models -> high-usage -> new quant modes.
2025-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/418 implements profile state machine and health webhook. Linked above.

2025-03-03 - PM follow-up: Add manual override path for stewards and an audit log entry for any archival transition (required for compliance). Confirming KMS-signed audit artifact requirement with Security.
2025-03-04 - Security (Asha Mehta): KMS audit signing OK; data retention policy for archived artifacts must be 2 years. Marked as added constraint in playbook.
2025-03-04 - Next steps: QA test plan, small canary rollout to internal models (catalog tags: internal-canary), prepare release notes for runtime-1.20 and Console-2025.03.
